inline.s: Exercise the meridians, and live healthy to a hundred.

The guiding theory of the 312 Meridian Health Method is the meridian theory of traditional Chinese medicine — namely, that most diseases of the body arise because the meridians are blocked, and that dysfunction of the meridians is the root cause of illness. Therefore, so long as the meridians are kept clear, the body will remain healthy and free of illness; unblocking the meridians can relieve pain, prevent and treat disease, and thereby prolong life.
• The 312 Meridian Health Method consists of massaging three acupoints (“
), one abdominal breathing exercise (“

) for health preservation. It frees you from the complexity of other health regimens, being simple and easy to practice, unrestricted by time or place, so that you can enjoy a century of health without ever leaving home.

• Verified by more than twenty years of practice, the 312 Meridian Health Method has restored health to tens of millions of people, won broad recognition from the public, and is a natural health method vigorously promoted by the General Administration of Sport of China.

• Each day, the 312 Meridian Health Method needs only 27 minutes of deliberate practice through three different means — acupoint massage, abdominal breathing, and squatting — to stimulate the meridian system in a planned way and bring the benefits of dispelling illness, strengthening the body, and prolonging life.
massage of three acupoints (Hegu, Neiguan, and Zusanli).

Method: press down and rub; once every two seconds, massage one acupoint for two minutes (about sixty to seventy presses). Either the left or right side is fine; do it once in the morning and once in the evening.

While massaging, if you feel soreness, numbness, and distension, and a sensation of qi coursing up and down, the massage is effective. Massage all three acupoints this way, six minutes in total. Twice a day makes twelve minutes.

The 312 Meridian Exercise Method

The ancients said: “Press Hegu, Neiguan, and Zusanli once a day and strengthen the whole body.” These three points are the three great acupoints that physicians of every age have used to strengthen the body and treat illness. Massage these three points, and if there is illness it will be cured; if there is none, the body will be strengthened.

Because nine meridians pass through the abdomen, abdominal breathing massages these nine meridians, ensuring the harmony of yin and yang among the five viscera and six bowels. At the same time it deepens the breath and increases the ventilation of the lungs (the supply of oxygen and the expulsion of carbon dioxide), thereby dispelling illness and prolonging life.
the two-legged squatting exercise.

Method: 1. Stand with the feet shoulder-width apart and the hands hanging down; 2. When squatting, raise both hands forward to shoulder level; 3. When rising, lower the hands and return to hanging at the sides (see
The 312 Meridian Exercise Method
). Squat and rise in this way, repeatedly. Do it

minutes, completing it in one session. The elderly and the weak may hold onto a table, a bedrail, or the like while doing it, and it will be just as effective. At first, do one minute a day, then gradually increase to five minutes a day; from doing it in several separate sessions, progress to completing it in one session, no longer holding onto anything.
The benefits of the squatting exercise:

When a person squats down, the body folds in three, the compressed blood vessels contract, and qi and blood rush into the body’s uncompressed vessels, forcing them to expand and swell; when the person stands up again, the qi and blood of the whole body rush back into the formerly compressed vessels, filling them with blood. In this back-and-forth movement of qi and blood — squatting and rising, pressing and releasing, rushing and returning — the vessels of the whole body are flushed again and again, like rinsing out a bottle. This softens the vessels, quickens the circulation of blood and the body’s metabolism, activates the immune system, increases high-density lipoprotein, sharpens the pressure receptors, and swiftly clears away harmful and toxic metabolic products.
At the same time,

the feet are the important starting and ending points of the twelve main meridians that circulate qi and blood, connect the viscera and bowels, link the interior and exterior, and run through the upper and lower body; together with the eight extraordinary vessels, the squatting exercise can naturally stimulate the qi of these nearly twenty channels.

Moreover, squatting increases the range of motion of the waist, hip, knee, and ankle joints, enhances the flexibility of the knees, and delays the aging of the joints. If the joints move little, the bones become fragile, calcium leaches into the blood, and it accumulates in the kidneys and bladder, causing difficulty in urination, the multiplication of bacteria, and other ill effects. So using and moving the joints often is the key to remaining youthful.
